continuity_scope: Jacqueline Carey, Kushiel's Dart, Tor/Macmillan edition, 15 March 2002, ISBN 9781429910903, 704 pages. This pass is one original-English novel only, using its numbered chapters rather than repaginated later-format pages. Kushiel's Chosen, Kushiel's Avatar, later Phedre/Imriel/Naamah works, Cassiel's Servant, companion fiction, adaptations, and author commentary are not story canon here.

coverage_rule: Include the first-person protagonist Phèdre; her named Delaunay household/mentors Anafiel, Alcuin, and Joscelin; companion Hyacinthe; central court figures Melisande, Ysandre, and Barquiel; and the named Skaldi and Alban leaders Waldemar Selig and Drustan mab Necthana. This ten-person cohort covers the household that forms the protagonist, her travelling partnership, the core political conspiracy and monarchy, and the leaders materially affecting the Skaldia/Alba conflict. Named patrons, nobles, House adepts, soldiers, clergy, captors, members of the Tsingani kumpania, and other minor figures are omitted.
omissions: All sequels, later trilogies, companion/retelling novels, short fiction, adaptations, games, author interviews, commentary, maps, and translations as independent continuities.
Named but non-cohort patrons, Court nobles, House personnel, Cassilines, Skaldi, Alba figures, sailors, prisoners, guards, and incidental historical figures.

Terre d'Ange, D'Angelines, the Night Court and Thirteen Houses, the service of Naamah, Elua and the Companions, Kushiel's mark, Cassiline Brotherhood, nations/peoples, social offices, magic, marques, artifacts, places, and institutions as character nodes.
uncertainties: Phèdre narrates in the first person. Her perception, attraction, interpretation of religious language, and political inference are not silently promoted to an external omniscient account.

The novel's sacred and sexual vocabulary is fictional and context-sensitive. A voluntary adult Naamah service/assignation, a coerced or enslaved sexual context, romantic attachment, and politically instrumental intimacy are not flattened into one category.

The book includes consensual adult sexual content, BDSM-coded desire, indenture, sexual coercion and violence, slavery, abuse, torture, murder, war, and trauma. Records avoid explicit detail and do not endorse coercion.
D'Angeline, Skaldi, Alba, Tsingani, and other terms may evoke historical/cultural material, but no one-to-one real-world ethnicity, nation, religion, or sexual-practice equivalence is asserted.

The Tor site provides an authorized Chapter One/Two excerpt; Google Books is a limited preview. Exact chapter locators are therefore retained and no later work is used to resolve ambiguity or outcome.
